title: [Livestream 10/1/2025] The proportion of energy produced from different resources in a country
prompt: The charts below show changes in the proportion of energy produced from different resources in a country in 1985 and 2003. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the changes in the proportion of various energy sources used in a country between 1985 and 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, natural gas and nuclear power saw significant declines in their proportions, whereas there were considerable increases in the shares of oil, coal, and other renewable sources, and hydrogen's figure remained stable throughout the period. Additionally, natural gas maintained its position as the dominant energy source in both years, despite its substantial decrease.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the major energy sources, natural gas accounted for more than half of the total energy production in 1985, at 52%, while oil contributed 13%. By 2003, the proportion of energy generated from natural gas had fallen to 39%, whereas that of oil rose significantly to 23%. Meanwhile, nuclear power and coal made up 22% and 8% of energy generated in 1985 respectively, but by the end of the period, coal's share had nearly tripled to 22%, while nuclear power's contribution decreased considerably to 8%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining energy sources, hydrogen constituted 4% of total energy production in 1985, and this figure remained unchanged in 2003. In contrast, other renewable sources, which accounted for merely 1% of energy generation in 1985, experienced a fourfold increase to 4% by the end of the period.
